content.text:
1) Answer

Short answer: Yes—there is clear, documented evidence across Lisa Nandy’s parliamentary speeches, questions, and votes, as well as cross‑party advocacy, that she consistently prioritises human rights.

Evidence highlights:
- Condemned mass abuses against Uyghur Muslims and pressed for stronger action and sanctions; spoke in the Commons framing Xinjiang atrocities as “barbaric” and urging concrete UK measures. ([hansard.parliament.uk](https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2021-03-22/debates/7E304076-1DAF-482C-B4AD-FFFDB8813E53/HumanRightsUpdate?utm_source=openai))
- Repeatedly defended civil and political rights in Hong Kong: challenged ministers after Beijing’s national security law, welcomed suspending UK–HK extradition, and pushed for coordinated international responses. ([hansard.parliament.uk](https://hansard.parliament.uk/commons/2020-07-01/debates/bb799e4f-923c-41ab-9cde-fb033031bd1a/CommonsChamber?utm_source=openai))
- Pressed the government to apply Magnitsky‑style sanctions to Hong Kong leaders and to call for a UN special rapporteur on Hong Kong, emphasising protection of fundamental freedoms. ([questions-statements.parliament.uk](https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-questions/detail/2021-06-22/20602?utm_source=openai))
- Co‑signed a cross‑party letter (with over 100 MPs/Peers) urging sanctions on Hong Kong officials and calling to expand sanctions for gross human rights abuses against Uyghurs. ([hongkongwatch.org](https://www.hongkongwatch.org/all-posts/2021/4/14/patten-led-group-of-over-100-mps-peers-call-for-sanctions-on-hk-officials?utm_source=openai))
- Sought to embed human rights in UK trade policy by asking ministers to include binding human‑rights clauses in a future UK–Israel agreement, citing the EU model. ([questions-statements.parliament.uk](https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-questions/detail/2019-07-01/271554?utm_source=openai))
- Opposed the Safety of Rwanda (Asylum and Immigration) Bill—legislation criticised for disapplying parts of the Human Rights Act and limiting ECHR interim measures—by voting against it at Commons stages. ([publicwhip.org.uk](https://www.publicwhip.org.uk/mp.php?id=uk.org.publicwhip%2Fmember%2F42875&showall=yes&utm_source=openai))
- As Shadow International Development in 2024, urged restoring UNRWA support and stressed accountability via international law in the Gaza crisis—placing humanitarian obligations and legal norms at the centre of UK policy. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/apr/17/lisa-nandy-urges-support-un-relief-agency-for-palestinians?utm_source=openai))
- As a cabinet minister (2025), publicly affirmed the duty to report on and protect journalists and highlighted the plight of children in Gaza during a Commons session—again signalling rights‑based concerns. ([hansard.parliament.uk](https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2025-02-27/debates/89B386F6-B5B4-4013-B810-B1F4A4A1C741/details?utm_source=openai))
- Used parliamentary scrutiny to advance women’s and LGBT+ rights, rule of law, press freedom and asylum‑seekers’ rights in the context of UK–Hungary relations. ([questions-statements.parliament.uk](https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-questions/detail/2021-06-08/12129?utm_source=openai))
- Maintained oversight of the UK’s Preventing Sexual Violence in Conflict Initiative, pressing ministers on delivery and resourcing. ([questions-statements.parliament.uk](https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-questions/detail/2024-03-26/20623?utm_source=openai))

Taken together—rights‑focused speeches and questions, cross‑party human‑rights advocacy, and voting to protect domestic and international human‑rights safeguards—these actions substantiate that Lisa Nandy values human rights.

2) Sources I considered trustworthy (with why)

- Source: UK Parliament (Hansard)
  - Reasoning 1: Official, verbatim record of parliamentary proceedings; non‑partisan and authoritative.
  - Reasoning 2: Primary evidence of Nandy’s own words on Xinjiang, Hong Kong, and Gaza-related matters. ([hansard.parliament.uk](https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2021-03-22/debates/7E304076-1DAF-482C-B4AD-FFFDB8813E53/HumanRightsUpdate?utm_source=openai))

- Source: UK Parliament (Written Questions/Statements)
  - Reasoning 1: Official record of MPs’ questions and ministerial answers; formally vetted and archived.
  - Reasoning 2: Directly shows Nandy asking for human‑rights‑related action (Hungary rights; Magnitsky on HK; UN rapporteur; PSVI). ([questions-statements.parliament.uk](https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-questions/detail/2021-06-08/12129?utm_source=openai))

- Source: UK Parliament (Votes in Parliament)
  - Reasoning 1: Official division results; definitive for what the House decided.
  - Reasoning 2: Confirms the context and outcomes of Rwanda Bill divisions (the bill’s rights implications). ([votes.parliament.uk](https://votes.parliament.uk/Votes/Commons?FromDate=16%2F01%2F2023&SearchText=safety+of+rwanda&ToDate=17%2F01%2F2024&utm_source=openai))

- Source: The Public Whip (mySociety)
  - Reasoning 1: Non‑profit that ingests official division lists and maps them to MPs; widely used for vote tracking.
  - Reasoning 2: Provides MP‑specific record showing Nandy voted “No” on the Rwanda Bill—consistent with Parliament’s own tallies. ([publicwhip.org.uk](https://www.publicwhip.org.uk/mp.php?id=uk.org.publicwhip%2Fmember%2F42875&showall=yes&utm_source=openai))

- Source: Hong Kong Watch
  - Reasoning 1: UK‑based human‑rights NGO focused on Hong Kong; publishes primary documents (letters) with signatories.
  - Reasoning 2: Hosts the cross‑party sanctions letter listing Nandy as a co‑signatory—direct evidence of rights advocacy. ([hongkongwatch.org](https://www.hongkongwatch.org/all-posts/2021/4/14/patten-led-group-of-over-100-mps-peers-call-for-sanctions-on-hk-officials?utm_source=openai))

- Source: The Guardian
  - Reasoning 1: Established UK newspaper with editorial standards and on‑the‑record sourcing.
  - Reasoning 2: Reported Nandy’s 2024 advocacy to restore UNRWA funding and emphasise international‑law accountability—relevant to her human‑rights stance. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/apr/17/lisa-nandy-urges-support-un-relief-agency-for-palestinians?utm_source=openai))

3) Sources I considered not trustworthy (and did not rely on)

- Source: Tasnim News Agency
  - Reasoning 1: Iranian state‑affiliated outlet; known government alignment raises concerns about independence and propaganda.
  - Reasoning 2: Its piece criticising UK politicians’ Gaza stances was not used because it offered no primary evidence about Nandy’s actions and had a high risk of bias for this prompt. ([tasnimnews.com](https://www.tasnimnews.com/en/news/2023/10/23/2976641/amnesty-accuses-uk-politicians-of-downplaying-gravity-of-gaza-human-rights-violations?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Indy100
  - Reasoning 1: Pop‑news/viral site associated with The Independent; lighter editorial model, often summarising clips.
  - Reasoning 2: A short item about Nandy’s Rwanda comments was not treated as proof; I relied instead on primary voting records and Hansard. ([indy100.com](https://www.indy100.com/politics/lisa-nandy-rwanda-suella-braverman?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Parallel Parliament
  - Reasoning 1: Unofficial mirror of Hansard; generally accurate but not the authoritative record.
  - Reasoning 2: I cross‑checked its excerpts against the official Hansard and did not use it as a primary citation. ([parallelparliament.co.uk](https://www.parallelparliament.co.uk/mp/lisa-nandy/debate/2023-12-04/commons/commons-chamber/gaza-humanitarian-situation?utm_source=openai))

If you want, I can compile a one‑page dossier with the key quotes and vote lines for archiving.
